subject: Week 46: book the 12-month well visit — May 10-26, five vaccines due
bodyText:
This week
Days 320–326: standing alone momentarily for many (CDC checkpoint: 12 months) and a few unassisted steps for some — the walks-alone checkpoint sits at 15 months. Language is where the 12-month checkpoint gets specific: mama and dada aimed at the right parent count as first words, while words beyond that sit at the 15-month checkpoint, so their absence now is expected rather than a flag. Tool use is emerging — he will drag a string to reach the toy tied to the end of it.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Day-to-day appetite swings of 40% in either direction — intake averages out over the week at this age.
- [monitor] No babble and no words at all as the visit approaches — top of the question list, in writing.
- [monitor] During bottle weaning: refusal of all milk substitutes for more than a few days, or a flat weight trend.
- [call within 24h] New wheezing, or any illness persisting past three days.
- [call now] Labored breathing with retractions, fever ≥102°F rectal with lethargy, or unresponsiveness — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Start the bottle-weaning sequence — replace one daytime bottle per week with a meal plus an open or straw cup, saving the pre-bed bottle for last; AAP guidance is off the bottle by 12–18 months, and the documented costs of running long are iron deficiency and dental caries.
- Log what mama and dada currently mean — use directed at the right parent is the CDC 12-month language checkpoint, and a week of notes gives the pediatrician better data than recall at the visit. CDC 12-month milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
- Engineer momentary standing: stand him at the couch and hand him a toy that needs both hands — the let-go moment is the checkpoint behavior, and he finds it on his own when his hands are busy. AAP: milestones at 12 months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
- Practice give-and-take — ask for the block, thank him, hand it back; giving an object on request is a 12-month social behavior and doubles as early turn-taking.

Upcoming
- Day 364–380 (May 10–26, 2027): 12-month well visit — book now. Vaccines: MMR #1, VAR #1, HepA #1, PCV #4, Hib booster; plus hemoglobin, lead screen, and first dental guidance. Mild fever or rash 7–12 days after MMR/VAR is common and not contagious.
- Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first birthday — final headcount and day-of timeline over the next two weeks.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Stands alone for a few seconds
  AAP window: day 300-365
  What to look for: Often follows cruising. Balance precedes locomotion.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/stands-briefly-no-support/complete

- Uses objects appropriately (cup, phone, book)
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: Functional use — picks up phone and puts it to ear, holds book the right way. Pretend play emerges from here.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-objects-appropriately/complete

- Takes a few steps on her own
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: CDC checkpoint is 15 months. Wide normal range — late walking alone is not concerning if other milestones are on track.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-independent-steps/complete

- Uses one word besides mama or dada
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: Commonly 'ball', 'dog', 'bye', or a family-specific word.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-one-word/complete

- Tries to imitate words you say
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: Approximations count. 'Wa' for water is a real attempt.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tries-to-imitate-words/complete
